t: pyproject.toml: one file to rule deps
title: pyproject.toml: one file to rule deps
description: Both tools center on pyproject.toml declaring dependencies, dev groups, and build config per PEP 518/621. One file replaces setup.py + requirements.txt sprawl. Declarative metadata is the modern standard.

title: Lockfiles: reproducible installs
description: Poetry.lock and uv.lock pin exact versions (and hashes) so installs reproduce bit-for-bit across machines. Commit the lockfile; CI installs from it. Reproducibility is the point of the lock.

demo.program: print('commit the lockfile; installs reproduce exactly')

title: Poetry: dependency resolution
description: Poetry's resolver finds a compatible version set across all constraints, reporting conflicts clearly instead of installing broken combos. Resolution is Poetry's historic strength. Conflicts surface at solve time, not runtime.

demo.program: print('poetry lock  # resolve; conflicts reported clearly')

title: Lockfile sync in CI
description: CI runs uv sync --frozen or poetry install --no-root for exact-lock installs, failing on lockfile drift. Frozen installs make builds hermetic. Drift fails loudly.

title: Choosing Poetry vs uv
description: Poetry for mature all-in-one project management; uv for raw speed and pip-compatible workflows — many teams use uv for speed with pyproject metadata. Both beat bare pip+venv. The ecosystem converged on pyproject.
